entries.effect: the current token is the one instance that answers as current: it is its own copy, equals itself and codes as a singleton; the class has no other token to make, and a token made with alloc and init answers no coordinator; the class is there, so NSClassFromString answers it
entries.reason: a token and the pinning to it are carried, and what the port does with a pinned context is what the newest Core Data does for a store that keeps no generations - the pinning is answered YES and the read sees the latest rows. journal_mode=WAL is reachable on this release through NSSQLitePragmasOption, which is iOS 5 API the store carries, so the journal the store keeps by default is not the reason: whether a second connection's read stays on its snapshot after a write is the question, and it is asked of the release by tests/backports/device/coredata-wal-snapshot.m. The facts file says the same, with the measurement's own wording.

entries.effect: nil until a token was set, and the token that was set after; nothing else reads it
entries.reason: iOS 6 has no write-ahead log to read a snapshot from, so a context pinned to a query generation reads the latest rows, as the newest Core Data does for a store that keeps no generations, an in-memory store; the pinning is kept and nothing isolates

entries.effect: answers YES and keeps the token, nil unpinning; a context with no coordinator answers NO and the error 134060 that iOS 12 answers; the reads of the context are not isolated from later saves
